# Git View

Review, stage, commit and push the session repository's git changes from the
Harness conversation vi

中文
## What it does

A **Git** tab in the conversation view ring, after Trajectory. It reads the
repository the session i
s working in — no path to configure, no second UI.

- **Every project in the workspace** — the repositories around the working
directory, each with its

own branch, markers and commit. They are committed
separately, never across repositories. Projects w

ith nothing pending fold into
one row so the ones you are actually working on stay on screen.
- **Ch

ange groups** — conflicts, staged, unstaged and untracked, each with
folder rows that fold a whole s

ubtree and stage or discard it in one action.
- **Three ways to read a file** — whole file with the

changes marked, changes
only as a unified diff, or side by side. Remembered across sessions.
- **Edi

t and save** — open a working-tree file in the panel and write it back,
guarded by the version the r

ead returned.
- **Branches, stash, pull, sync** — and a fetch, refresh and discard group.
- **Commit

and push** — an AI-written commit message from the staged diff, a
commit button that commits, and a

push button that lists every commit it would
publish before it publishes them.

Untracked directories stay folded until opened, and opening one asks git about
that directory alone.

A working tree with twenty thousand untracked files costs
the same to list as one with twenty.

A repository nested inside another one is not offered as a folder in its
parent's file list, because

git will not describe what is inside it to the
parent and opening one would show nothing. It is one
of the projects instead.

Requires dsh 0.2.0-rc.2 or newer, Node 22.19+ or 24+, and a session whose
